answer: We analyze a decentralized nebula where validator identities branch along a cryptographic vine of sequential delay proofs. To manipulate consensus, any malicious Sybil cluster must commit a compressed pearl representing a quadratic slashing risk on their locked staking collateral. Because the penalty scales quadratically with correlated validation faults, the marginal attack cost grows super-linearly, guaranteeing a negative expected utility that sustains a robust Nash equilibrium.
